title: Programming IME local core JSON Lines protocol 0.3
description: stdin/stdout JSON Lines between a trusted local process and pime-core: one JSON object per line, exactly one response line per request line. Every request may carry an integer `id` that is echoed in the response as `id`. Protocol 0.3 is a SUPERSET of 0.2 (schemas/core-protocol-v0.2.json): the seven stateless 0.2 operations behave exactly as before and keep the 65536 byte line limit; `health` now reports protocol "0.3" (and the unchanged version "0.2.0"); `predict` additionally accepts the optional `pins` and `usage` ranking inputs. The stateful operations below are new. Every new operation except `session.open` names an open session in `session`; a missing, unknown, evicted or expired session answers NO_SESSION. Operations that carry document text (ctx.snapshot, ctx.validate, edit.propose, edit.plan, edit.prepare, edit.begin_apply, edit.finish_apply) may use lines up to 16777216 bytes; every other operation is limited to 65536 bytes (PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE otherwise). All offsets and columns are UTF-16 code units. The core keeps snapshot and proposal text in memory (addressed by snapshot_id / proposal) so the bridge never resends it; ids are derived from the `entropy` given to session.open (HMAC-SHA-256 counter construction, see crates/pime-core/src/ids.rs). Time comes from the core's wall clock (epoch milliseconds). New top-level request fields are snake_case; nested objects that mirror the bridge's own shapes keep their camelCase names. The core never executes anything, never opens files or the network and never echoes secret values. Migration steps 1.2 and 1.3 add, without changing anything above: ai.prompt, ai.prepare, ai.complete, ai.parse (provider request construction and response/error handling; the HTTP call itself stays with the sender), privacy.assess / redact / restore / release, annotate.supports / prompt / f1_addendum / apply, symbols.extract / dir_candidates, and sched.* / lang.* (realtime scheduling decisions and input session epochs and locks). Of these, ai.prompt, ai.prepare, ai.complete, ai.parse, privacy.assess, privacy.redact, privacy.restore, annotate.prompt, annotate.apply, symbols.extract and lang.state may also use lines up to 16777216 bytes. Not the secure PIME-IPC/1 named-pipe protocol of the detailed design.

id.description: Optional correlation id, echoed verbatim as `id` in the response. A non-integer id is rejected with INVALID_REQUEST (field `id`).

session.description: Session id returned by session.open (32 lowercase hex characters).

dialect.description: Dialect axis -> value, for example {"edition":"2021"}. Values must be strings (or null = default).

edit.description: A replacement of [start, end) of the baseline text (UTF-16 offsets). Offsets must not split a surrogate pair or a CRLF; edits must not overlap; two inserts at one offset are ambiguous.

docState.description: The document as the editor reports it right now. The core hashes `text` itself. null or absent counts as a closed document.

grant.description: The grant object exactly as the JavaScript broker keeps and persists it (key pime.grants.v1).

workspaceRef.description: Exactly one of `workspace` (a token) or `workspace_uris` (the workspace folder uris; the core derives the token: first 24 hex characters of SHA-256 of the uris sorted by UTF-16 code unit and joined by \n).

pins.description: 0.3: candidate ids that always rank first.

usage.description: 0.3: candidate id -> local use count (tie-break before weight).

sessionOpenRequest.description: Opens a session. `entropy` is 32..512 bytes of cryptographically random data (hex) from the caller (crypto.randomBytes): the core has no entropy source of its own (a limitation that phase P2 removes with the OS random generator). A buffer with fewer than 8 distinct byte values is refused, and the same entropy cannot open two sessions. At most 16 sessions are kept (the least recently used is dropped) and a session idle for 24 hours expires.

settingsValues.description: The bridge's configuration values: {providers, scenarios, budget} (each an object). Unknown scenarios and invalid provider ids are dropped, user values override the defaults field by field.

ctxSnapshotRequest.description: Takes a snapshot of an editor buffer (never of the disk) and keeps its TEXT in the core. At most 8 snapshots (and 64 MiB of text) are kept per session; the oldest is dropped. Release it with ctx.release when the F1 session closes.

text.description: A missing or non-string text answers CONTEXT_UNAVAILABLE.

level.description: Context level L0-L4. Whole-file plans need L3; L4 (disk) is preview only.

ctxExcerptRequest.description: A nearby excerpt (L1) of a snapshot; the bounds never split a surrogate pair or a CRLF. With `policy`, a wider request than the authorised bounds answers GRANT_DENIED.

cursor.description: UTF-16 offset, clamped to the text

ctxValidateRequest.description: Syntax check of the snapshot text, or of the snapshot with `edits` applied (preview of an insert; nothing is created).

ctxReleaseRequest.description: Forgets a snapshot and every proposal made from it (source text must not linger).

editProposeRequest.description: Builds the line hunks that turn the snapshot into `proposed_text` and holds the proposal (text + hunks; at most 16 per session). A proposal is not a plan yet: the plan, with its lifetime, is created by edit.plan when the user applies.

language.description: With a language, every result carries the syntax verdict.

editSelectRequest.description: The result of applying the chosen hunks to the baseline (unknown hunk ids are ignored).

editResultRequest.description: The whole result text of a hunk selection (for the read-only Diff view). The reply may be as large as the document.

editPlanRequest.description: EditCoordinator.createPlan: a plan from the chosen hunks of a `proposal`, or from explicit `edits` of a snapshot (the insert path). Rules: kind full|insert, every target must be the snapshot's document (CROSS_FILE_DENIED), a full plan needs an L3 snapshot (FULL_CONTEXT_REQUIRED), at least one edit, valid non-overlapping offsets. The plan lives 10 minutes.

editPrepareRequest.description: EditCoordinator.prepare, checked in this order: plan exists (TOKEN_INVALID), `confirmed` is the literal true (USER_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED), the grant is still valid (GRANT_DENIED), then the plan is not stale / expired / unknown-result (STALE_DOCUMENT, STALE_RESULT, EDIT_UNKNOWN), the document is open (DOCUMENT_CLOSED), uri + version + SHA-256 of `state.text` equal the baseline (STALE_DOCUMENT), writable (EDIT_REJECTED), an insert's selection is unchanged (STALE_SELECTION), and finally `validation_ok` is not false (VALIDATION_FAILED). Returns a one-use token valid for 60 seconds.

grant_id.description: The core asks its own broker (still valid: not revoked, not expired; a used one-request grant still counts).

grant_ok.description: Used only when `grant_id` is absent; only the literal true counts.

validation_ok.description: Only the literal false disables the apply.

editBeginApplyRequest.description: First half of apply: re-validates the plan against `state`, marks the token used BEFORE anything is written and returns the edits to write as ONE editor edit (one Undo). Starts a deadline of apply_timeout_ms. While another write of the same document waits for its result, a second begin answers EDIT_REJECTED without consuming its token.

editFinishApplyRequest.description: Second half of apply: what the editor answered and the document state after the write. accepted -> the SHA-256 of state.text must equal the plan's proposed hash (APPLIED, otherwise EDIT_UNKNOWN); rejected -> EDIT_REJECTED when the document is still the baseline, otherwise EDIT_UNKNOWN; error (the editor threw, or the bridge gave up) -> EDIT_UNKNOWN. A finish after the deadline is EDIT_UNKNOWN, never APPLIED. EDIT_UNKNOWN is final: it is never retried automatically and the plan cannot be prepared again.

editInvalidateRequest.description: The document changed, closed or lost focus: every REVIEW_READY or PREPARED plan of the uri becomes STALE.

editPurgeRequest.description: Drops expired plans, used tokens and applied plans.

grantAuthorizeRequest.description: PermissionBroker.authorize. The reply carries `persist`: the reusable, not revoked grants for the bridge to store (pime.grants.v1). One-request grants (`once`) are never persisted.

grantCheckRequest.description: Any mismatch is a denial: reason is one of ok, unknown-grant, revoked, expired, already-used, provider-mismatch, workspace-mismatch, scope-mismatch.

grantFindRequest.description: A reusable (workspace-wide) grant for the criteria, or null.

grantRequireRequest.description: Like grant.check, but a denial is the error GRANT_DENIED "authorisation denied (<reason>)".

grantRevokeProviderPrefixRequest.description: Revokes every grant whose provider id starts with `prefix` ("<provider>:" = every host of one provider), used or expired ones included: no authorisation survives its key.

grantStillValidRequest.description: Honoured at Apply time: not revoked and not expired (a used one-request grant still counts).

grantListRequest.description: Live grants: not revoked, not expired, not a used one-request grant.

grantImportRequest.description: Loads persisted grants (at most 1000). Malformed entries (not an object, no string id, unknown scope, a one-request grant, non-string provider or workspace, no numeric expiry) are skipped.

budgetConfigureRequest.description: Limits and price; the counters keep running. A missing, null, zero or negative limit means unlimited (the bridge's 0).

budgetReserveRequest.description: Reserves one request and `estimate` tokens before anything is sent; AI_BUDGET_EXCEEDED when the budget is used up. Returns a ticket (at most 1024 unsettled ones).

budgetSettleRequest.description: Settles a ticket with the real usage, or with its estimate when `usage` is absent (the budget is then marked estimated). An unknown (already closed) ticket is a no-op: settled=false.

budgetReleaseRequest.description: Gives the reservation back (the request never happened).

inputKey.description: The identity of one input: any change of one field invalidates results tied to an older value (seq: keystrokes, profileEpoch: language switches, documentEpoch: document changes).

effects.description: What the bridge does: clear its debounce timer, abort the running request (best effort: data already sent cannot be recalled) and, when arm_ms is not null, start a new timer of that many milliseconds.

effortResult.description: The effort negotiation: `status` is omitted (auto), sent (value is the vendor value), unsupported, stale (capability older than 30 days) or unknown. Anything but omitted/sent says why the level was NOT sent in `message`.

aiPromptRequest.description: buildPrompt: the fixed, tool-less instructions of a task and the payload as the data channel (JSON.stringify(payload)); file text never reaches `instructions`.

payload.description: any JSON value (an object in practice)

aiPrepareRequest.description: Everything AiClient.infer does before the HTTP call, in the same order, so the first failing check is the same: AI_DISABLED, the 429 cool-down (AI_RATE_LIMIT), unknown family / no model (MODEL_UNSUPPORTED), the HTTPS endpoint (SETTINGS_INVALID), no key (VAULT_ERROR), authorisation by the core's own grants (untrusted workspace or no grant: CONSENT_REQUIRED; a given grant_id is required and consumed: GRANT_DENIED), the last sensitivity gate (SENSITIVE_BLOCKED unless allow_sensitive), the budget reservation (AI_BUDGET_EXCEEDED), then effort negotiation and the request. The key is only ever put into the returned headers. At most 64 prepared requests wait for their outcome (the oldest is settled as failed).

max_output_tokens.description: 0/absent: 800 in the request, 0 in the reservation

capability.description: the model's effort capability record; an unknown, stale or unverified capability means the effort parameter is NOT sent

aiCompleteRequest.description: The outcome of a prepared request, reported once: `transport_error` (the sender saw no usable answer), or `status` (+ `retry_after`, the raw Retry-After header: absent = the sender has no header API, null = no such header, otherwise the string) and the `body`. Non-2xx statuses map to AI_AUTH_FAILED / AI_QUOTA / AI_TIMEOUT / AI_RATE_LIMIT / AI_SERVER_ERROR / AI_BAD_REQUEST (a 429 pauses AI until the retry time, 30 s without one); a transport failure to AI_CANCELLED / AI_TIMEOUT / AI_NETWORK. A body over max_response_units UTF-16 units (or `oversize`:true, when the sender did not forward it), that is not JSON, or has no text is OUTPUT_INVALID. Every outcome settles the budget reservation: with the real usage, or with the estimate.

code.description: its code, or its cause's code

user_aborted.description: the user's own cancel signal had fired

aiParseRequest.description: parseModelResult: strict validation of a model reply (model output is data). A fenced reply is tolerated, unknown keys are listed in ignoredKeys and dropped, NUL is stripped, bounds (1 MiB reply, 500000-unit file, 8 candidates of 100000 units, 200 patch edits) are enforced, a cross-file plan keeps only the current file (the rest counts in rejectedTargets), a patch is applied to `baseline` (overlaps and surrogate splits are refused) and LF output for a CRLF baseline is converted (and announced in assumptions). A missing or non-string `raw` is OUTPUT_INVALID. A reply with duplicate keys or nesting deeper than 64 is OUTPUT_INVALID (the JSON parser is strict).

privacyAssessRequest.description: assessOutbound: what may leave the machine. allow (nothing found), redact (medium findings), and for high-risk content or a credential-like file name: block (scope realtime: never sent) or confirm (any other scope: the user must decide explicitly). Findings carry kind, severity and line, never the value.

privacyRedactRequest.description: Replaces every finding of `text` by a PIME_REDACTED_n marker (numbered from 1 per call) and keeps the originals in the core under a `redaction` id. Passing the id of an earlier reply adds the parts of one prompt to the same set (up to 16 sets per session, 100000 entries per set); markers that two parts share go to the later part, as in the reference. The originals are never returned.

privacyRestoreRequest.description: Puts the originals of a redaction set back into a model reply; a marker that is not in the set stays and is counted in `unresolved` (the bridge must not use such a reply).

privacyReleaseRequest.description: Forgets a redaction set (the originals must not linger).

annotateSupportsRequest.description: Whether annotation is supported for a language and its line-comment prefix (assembly: ; or # for gas).

annotatePromptRequest.description: buildAnnotatePrompt: the instructions ask for what is enabled (comment and/or graph), the file text stays in the data channel.

annotateF1AddendumRequest.description: The text appended to the F1 instructions when autoComment / graphComment are on (empty when neither is on or the language has no line comments).

annotateApplyRequest.description: applyAnnotateReply: the AI may only ADD comments. The commented snippet is accepted only if, after removing comments and collapsing whitespace (Python keeps indentation), it equals the original (otherwise note comment-rejected:<reason>); a `${` inside a comment is neutralised (it would become a snippet tab stop); Cypher lines are re-rendered with the language's own comment prefix after sanitising (MERGE/MATCH/CREATE only, no DELETE/DETACH/DROP/LOAD CSV/CALL, at most 12 lines of 300 characters). An unusable reply returns the original (note reply-invalid).

symbolsExtractRequest.description: The heuristic symbol index of one file (names only: declarations per language, comments and strings ignored, de-duplicated, file order, the first 200 KiB). max defaults to 60 and is capped at 1000.

symbolsDirCandidatesRequest.description: The decisions of the directory scan that need no file access: of a directory listing (at most 10000 entries) the regular files other than the current one, not credential-like by name, whose language the extension identifies, in listing order. The caller reads them and calls symbols.extract.

schedConfigureRequest.description: The debounce window of the realtime scheduler: clamped to 150..1000 ms; anything that is not a number is the default 350.

schedScheduleRequest.description: New input: it becomes the newest (every older one is stale at once) and the reply says what to do with the timer and the running request. `allowed` is the bridge's own gate (AI on, not paused, a grant): not allowed means no timer.

schedFireRequest.description: The debounce timer fired and the previous request has settled: start the request only if `start` is true (the input is still the newest and still allowed).

schedFinishRequest.description: A started request finished (ok) or failed (ok false, with the error code when it has one). The result is delivered only if its input is still the newest and the request was not aborted; otherwise it is discarded with STALE_RESULT.

schedCancelRequest.description: Forgets the newest input (nothing is stale-checked against it any more) and asks to stop the timer and the running request.

schedTouchRequest.description: Input session epochs: a keystroke (seq), a document change (documentEpoch) or a language switch (profileEpoch; `changed` says whether it really switched). Returns the current key.

schedIsCurrentRequest.description: Whether a key still equals the session's current key (null or an older key: false).

langStateRequest.description: InputSession.resolve: a manual lock always beats automatic detection and weak evidence never switches the profile; the session's language (and profile epoch) follows the decision.

file_key.description: a hash of the document uri, never a path

langLockRequest.description: Locks the profile for one file (file_key) or for everything (scope global). An unknown profile is refused: locked false. The reply lists the locks for persistence.

settingsValidateRequest.description: validateSettings: the problems of effective settings (the given ones, else the session's), each with its path. Effort levels: auto, none, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max, extended.

settings.description: Effective settings {providers, scenarios, budget}; the session settings when omitted.

settingsMigrateRequest.description: migrate (+ the document migrateStore writes): a v1 document passes through, a v0.1 flat one becomes the v1 structure (checkedAt from the core's clock), a newer schema_version answers SETTINGS_INVALID. `document` is what a store should hold afterwards: fields the settings do not own are kept, the legacy flat keys are retired.

settingsExportRequest.description: exportSettings: the settings as pretty JSON (schema_version, providers, scenarios, budget). Anything secret-like in it answers SETTINGS_INVALID.

settingsImportRequest.description: importSettings: parse, migrate, merge with the defaults and validate; nothing is applied (the bridge writes the configuration). The request may be a long line.

settingsRulesCheckRequest.description: buildRegistryWithUserRules, validation only: every user rule pack is checked as data against the built-in rules; a bad pack is rejected with its code and message and skipped. The core keeps no registry (its predictions use the built-in rules). The request may be a long line.

text.description: A pack over 262144 bytes is rejected.

diagRecordRequest.description: Records one diagnostic event in the session's ring (500 events). Only these fields are kept: timestamp (a number, else the core's clock), component, error_code, error_detail, elapsed_ms, request_type, provider_id and counters; values must be short tokens ([A-Za-z0-9_.:-], at most 64 characters) or numbers, everything else becomes "[filtered]".

diagSummaryRequest.description: The ring summarised: total, counts by error code and the last result per component.

diagTextRequest.description: The ring as one JSON line per event, oldest first.

uiResolveLocaleRequest.description: resolveLocale: an explicit interface locale wins, otherwise the editor language (zh* -> zh-CN, ja* -> ja-JP, anything else en-US).

setting.description: zh-CN, en-US or ja-JP; any other value (auto) defers to the language.

language.description: The editor language; en when omitted. Any non-string reads as String(value).

uiTextRequest.description: An interface text by key: {0}, {1}, ... are replaced in one pass by the arguments (null is empty, other values read as String(value)); an unknown key answers itself; a missing translation reads English.

locale.description: The interface locale; the session locale when omitted. Any other value reads English.

uiErrorTextRequest.description: describeError: the sentence of a stable error code, else `message`, else the code itself.

locale.description: The interface locale; the session locale when omitted. Any other value reads English.

uiBundleRequest.description: A dictionary of interface texts: the asked keys, or all 104 when `keys` is omitted. Texts are rendered WITHOUT arguments (placeholders become empty) unless `raw` is true, which keeps {0}, {1}, ... so that a bridge can cache the templates and fill them itself. Integer-like keys come first.

locale.description: The interface locale; the session locale when omitted. Any other value reads English.

uiErrorsRequest.description: The sentence of every error code that has one (31), for one locale.

locale.description: The interface locale; the session locale when omitted. Any other value reads English.

uiCandidateRowsRequest.description: Candidate rows for the quick pick: label, description ([source] validation), detail, ariaLabel (n / total ...) and whether the candidate can be inserted. Meaning is carried by text, never by colour.

text.description: null or absent: the candidate cannot be inserted

locale.description: The interface locale; the session locale when omitted. Any other value reads English.

uiPlaceOverlayRequest.description: Places a candidate window inside the monitor work area that contains the caret (below the line, flipped above or clamped when there is no room). null when the caret is on no monitor or the window does not fit: hide, never steal focus.

dpi.description: Display scaling in percent, clamped to 100-250; 100 when omitted.

uiCheckEnvRequest.description: The environment check: Windows 11 (build >= 22000) on x64, display scaling 100-250 %. Fields that are missing or of another type count as unsupported (an omitted dpi is skipped).

uiStatusModelRequest.description: The two status bar items as plain text, from everything the extension knows when it redraws. The redraw itself is synchronous, so the bridge keeps its JS function; this operation is the ported, parity-tested equivalent.

core_down.description: The Rust engine's core is unavailable.

locale.description: The interface locale; the session locale when omitted. Any other value reads English.

uiMenuModelRequest.description: The status bar menu: a title and the items in order; the id is what the extension maps to its action. The AI item names the action and is English in every locale.

locale.description: The interface locale; the session locale when omitted. Any other value reads English.

hunk.description: Geometry in 1-based lines and UTF-16 offsets plus the display lines (kind ' ', '-' or '+'; two lines of context).

length.description: UTF-16 units of the result text

settings.description: The effective settings in the JS shape (key order follows JavaScript object spread).

snapshot.description: The JS snapshot fields without `content` (the core keeps the text).

cost.description: null when no price is configured

http.description: POST body (a JSON object) and headers to send to url; redirects must not be followed (the credential header must never reach another host).

usage.description: null when the reply had no usable (non-negative integer) token counts

code.description: with discard: STALE_RESULT, the error code of the request, or ERROR

document.description: What a settings store holds after the migration.

event.description: The sanitised event as stored; fields in the order timestamp, component, error_code, error_detail, elapsed_ms, request_type, anonymized_session, provider_id, counters.

oneOf.title: success without data (session.close, grant.consume, budget.configure, budget.reset, edit.discard, edit.purge)

field.description: INVALID_REQUEST: the offending request field (nested fields as a.b).

message.description: Never contains document text, prompts or credentials.

retryable.description: AI failures (ai.prepare / ai.complete): the metadata of the reference error.

user_action.description: AI failures: what the user can do (may be empty).

retry_after_sec.description: AI_RATE_LIMIT from ai.complete: the provider's Retry-After in seconds, when it gave a finite one.

detail.description: AI_NETWORK: a sanitised transport code such as ECONNREFUSED, never text from the exchange.

budget.description: AI failures: the budget after the failure was settled.

oneOf.title: encode / validate_hex refusal (unchanged from 0.2; no bytes are ever returned)
